examShortTricks: Trick 1: Moyn's critique: the human-rights movement rose while inequality exploded — rights to minimal dignity have not checked market excess; state the paradox.
Trick 2: The historical arc: 1940s welfare nationalism → 1970s minimalist rights — the timeline is the essay's spine.
Trick 3: His challenge: rights talk must tackle distribution, not just torture and speech — quote the redistribution demand.
practiceQuestions: Q. What paradox does Moyn identify? (2 marks) — human rights triumphed globally at the same time as inequality reached historic highs.
Q. What must the rights movement do next, according to Moyn? (2 marks) — address economic distribution and material equality.
keyPoints: Human rights rose as inequality soared — they coexist uneasily; know this paradox.
Moyn criticises rights' minimalism: sufficiency is not equality; explain the gap.
